_notes: Baseline/default store — relies on code defaults in store.js (no plp.selectors/pdp.selectors/branding.footer). July 2 2026: sort label corrected to the live wording "Price: Low to High" (hash #/ps:calculated_price:asc re-verified live — the ps: prefix is correct for this older SearchSpring template); contact/quote/proClub submitUrlPatterns tightened to named Zoho forms (BESTContactUs, BESTRequestQuote1, BestAccessDoorsProClubVIPProgramApplication). PRO CLUB (July 14 2026): the live country dropdown offers -Select- / Canada / United States; the Canada option is an intentional fallback (a Canadian applicant who submits gets an error screen linking to the CA Pro Club form), NOT a region-lock defect, so no allowedCountries restriction is set (the 'offers only allowed countries' test in pro-club-form.cy.js is gated off). personaOverrides gives all BESTUS form tests a US address (the shared personas.json primary address is Canadian). KNOWN DEFICIENCY (July 23 2026, skipped for now — forms.proClub.emailErrorNotVisible): the Pro Club form correctly blocks submission when Email is empty, but the Email_error message never toggles visible (verified live: style stays display:none 1.5s+ after submit) — a Zoho form-config gap isolated to this one field on this one form. pro-club-form.cy.js gates only the visible-error assertion on this flag; the functional no-submission check still runs unconditionally. Revisit once the Zoho form (BestAccessDoorsProClubVIPProgramApplication) is fixed. KNOWN DEFICIENCY (July 23 2026, skipped for now): /content/assets/js/tracking_code.js — loaded only on /request-a-quote/ — is deployed with literal <script>/</script> wrapper tags still inside the file content (a Zoho UTM/lead-tracking snippet meant for inline embedding, mistakenly saved as a standalone external file). Loaded via <script src>, the browser parses the raw text as JS and chokes on the leading '<' (SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<', no stack — same shape as a redacted cross-origin error). Confirmed low-severity: the real Zoho form/submission is unaffected (manual submit works fine) — only this script's own UTM-attribution cookie logic silently never runs on that page. quote-form.cy.js suppresses this one known error via checks.js's KNOWN_BUGGY_SCRIPTS list. Fix means re-uploading tracking_code.js without the wrapper tags, or embedding the snippet inline instead of via external src. RECAPTCHA (Sept 1 2026): /contact-us/ (sitekey 6Lc19yct...) and /pro-club-application/ (sitekey 6Leol0gt...) now render a Google reCAPTCHA v2 checkbox plus a first-party inline gate — a submit listener that preventDefault()s while grecaptcha.getResponse() === ''. Intentional anti-spam, not a defect, but a v2 checkbox cannot be solved by an automated run (nor by a human mid-run), so on /contact-us/ it blocked every POST and contact-form.cy.js's 3 happy-path tests failed with cy.wait('@submit') 'No request ever occurred' — while every validation test kept passing, because Zoho's own onSubmit attribute handler (zf_ValidateAndSubmit) runs upstream of the gate. checks.js's THIRD_PARTY_HOSTS now stubs /recaptcha/ with a grecaptcha stand-in returning a non-empty token so the gate falls through; forms.contact.hasRecaptcha / forms.proClub.hasRecaptcha record which forms carry it and enable the 'does not submit until the reCAPTCHA is completed' test. Neither the quote form nor the PDP product forms are gated, and no other store in the fleet is (all 23 configured form pages scanned Sept 1 2026) — likely a rollout in progress, so re-scan for the widget when another store's happy path starts failing this way. GATE FRAGILITY (not a current defect, but the reason the enforcement test exists): the snippet installs its submit listener on document.getElementById('zohoForm'), so it does nothing at all unless the form's id matches. On Sept 1 2026 the /pro-club-application/ form was id='form' while contact's was already id='zohoForm' — 'if (!form) return' short-circuited, the widget rendered, and that captcha blocked nothing. Fixed overnight (confirmed by the store owner) and re-checked Sept 2 2026: the id is now 'zohoForm' (5 cache-busted fetches, no HTML variants — not an A/B variant) and the gate enforces — pro-club-form.cy.js's 'does not submit until the reCAPTCHA is completed' test passes. Neither state is visible in the page, so a one-word template edit can disarm the captcha silently; that test is the only thing that would catch it. CHECKOUT (Sept 14 2026): checkout.cy.js drives the funnel to the payment step. Live-verified facts worth keeping: /checkout 302s to /cart.php on an empty cart (so the spec must prove the cart is populated first); this storefront answers 406 to any HTML route requested with a wildcard Accept header, which is cy.request's default, so cy.request is only ever pointed at /api/ paths here; the checkout steps are <li class='checkout-step--customer|shipping|billing|payment'>, NOT '#checkout-<step>' ids; billing is auto-skipped because #sameAsBilling ships checked; and selecting a country REPLACES input#provinceInput with select#provinceCodeInput. The configured checkout.product adds TWO physical line items (the panel plus a zero-price latch component — BigCommerce's own cart API rejects the product as 'requires modifier options' without them), which is why the post-sign-in basket check compares against a count captured before sign-in rather than a hardcoded 1. The step containers' 'active' class is CUMULATIVE (steps reached, not the one expanded): after sign-in the customer step still has it and shipping does not, despite the shipping form being rendered and fillable, and all four flip to active together at the end — so it is an ordering signal only, and assertPaymentStep additionally asserts the visible 'Place Order' button. SHIPPING STEP HAS TWO SHAPES (Sept 15 2026): with an empty customer address book BigCommerce renders a blank address form; with anything saved it renders a saved-address dropdown (a#addressToggle) and #countryCodeInput does not exist at all. This account is SHARED - its address book held 28 entries from other teams' manual testing as of Sept 15 2026 - so the shape is not under the spec's control, and an earlier version that accepted the saved address as-is was testing whatever address a colleague last typed. fillShippingAddress now switches to a blank form via chooseNewAddress(). Live-verified mechanics: the menu is ul#addressDropdown (named by the toggle's aria-controls), is NOT in the DOM until the toggle is clicked and is NOT a descendant of the toggle's parent, so it must be found by its own id; 'Enter a new address' carries data-test='add-new-address' and is the FIRST item, above every saved address, so the 185px scrolling menu never needs paging however large the book grows; the dropdown is NOT touched until the preselected address has been quoted (waitForShippingQuote then waitForCheckoutIdle), which is what cured the RequestError: Consignment not found that defeated the earlier attempt - a rendered quote is the only proof the consignment exists server-side; and 'Save this address in my address book' (input[name='shippingAddress.shouldSaveAddress']) already ships UNCHECKED, so ensureSaveAddressUnchecked() is a guard, kept strict (should('exist')) because a drifted selector would silently start adding one address per run to a shared account. The count is logged every run and MUST NOT GROW between two back-to-back runs (verified: 28 -> 28); the absolute number means nothing. assertAddressHeld() then proves the address took - a revert restores the picker and removes #countryCodeInput (it cannot key on a#addressToggle, which stays in the DOM on BOTH shapes); if the blank form never arrives the spec logs '!! FALLBACK' and continues on the saved address rather than going red, so a green run is not by itself proof the address was controlled. KNOWN DEFICIENCY (Sept 15 2026, storefront's own code - devs should fix): the /checkout page template binds an inline jQuery click handler to the address-dropdown <li> items which, at /checkout line 956, does console.log('Radio button clicked:', selected.value) where selected = document.querySelector("input[name='shippingAddress.customFields.field_36']:checked"). Clicking 'Enter a new address' resets the form so nothing is checked, selected is null, and the handler throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'value') - which a REAL CUSTOMER hits on the same click. It is non-blocking for the address form itself, but it aborts the rest of that handler including its own checkShippingMethods_2(fullAddress2, 'Yes') call at line 967, so the store's construction-site shipping filter never runs on the new-address path. Fix is a null guard before line 956 (the handler also ships with leftover debug console.log calls: 'AL', 'H2', 'Construction002'). Suppressed only for the duration of that one click and only for a stack frame on the /checkout document (CheckoutPage.chooseNewAddress), never via KNOWN_BUGGY_SCRIPTS - 'Cannot read properties of null' is the most common shape of a real regression and a global entry for it would blind the suite. Every suppressed error is re-logged by name and source line. FALSIFIED (Sept 15 2026): with personaOverrides.zip temporarily set to 00000, all 3 attempts failed at selectShippingMethod with zero shipping options quoted (60s timeout each) - so BESTUS quotes carrier-validated shipping and this flow genuinely depends on a valid postcode. Separately, no-oping fillZip made assertAddressHeld fail at 5a/6 with expected '77001', actual '' - the guard itself fires. Cart cleanup must live in afterEach, NOT after(): with the same body, after() logs 'deleted 0 cart(s)' and afterEach logs 'deleted 1' — Cypress tears the session down before an after() all-hook runs, and because carts are session-scoped the resulting orphan is invisible even to a later signed-in API call, so the failure looks exactly like success. checkout.customFields answers 'Is this a construction site address? (Required)' — a BigCommerce custom field with no `required` attribute, only '(Required)' in its label text, which silently blocks the carrier quote when left blank. CONSOLE (calibrated Sept 14 2026, left gated off): checkout.consoleIgnore is null, so the console-error test is a documented skip. The page emits 3 console.error calls — 2 are paypal_js_sdk_v5_unhandled_exception (PayPal's SDK racing the guest-to-sign-in form swap; also suppressed as a KNOWN_BUGGY_SCRIPTS stackPattern) and the 3rd is a bare console.error(undefined) with no message or origin. Ignoring 'paypal_js_sdk_v5' alone takes it 3 -> 1; the remaining one cannot be matched without an ignore of 'undefined', which would swallow every future 'Cannot read properties of undefined' — the most common real regression — so the test stays skipped rather than becoming vacuous. Revisit if the undefined call is ever traced. PAYMENT STEP + ORDER PLACEMENT (Sept 15 2026): the payment step was calibrated by dumping GET /api/storefront/checkouts/<cartId> (the checkout id IS the cart id) and the rendered step markup. Totals on this account are subtotal 0 + shipping 26.04 + handling 0 + tax 2.15 - discount 0 = grandTotal 28.19, and they reconcile exactly. SUBTOTAL IS LEGITIMATELY 0: the QA customer's group carries a price list that zeroes the product (listPrice/salePrice 0 against originalPrice 180.69, retailPrice 252.98), so what is actually payable is shipping + tax — never 'fix' this by asserting subtotal > 0. BigCommerce AUTO-APPLIES store credit: #useStoreCredit ships CHECKED with label 'Apply $28.19 store credit to order', isStoreCreditApplied is true and outstandingBalance is 0 with no interaction at all, so nothing needs to click it. orderId is null until an order exists, which is a stronger 'no order was placed' signal than the URL check. The payment step offers five gateways as ul.form-checklist > li.form-checklist-item (paypalcommerce, paypalcommercecredit, paypalcommercecreditcards, amazonpay, googlepay) and renders [data-test='payment-store-credit-overlay'] — 'Payment is not required for this order.' — OVER them. That overlay is the load-bearing interlock for utils/placeOrder.js: a credit-card method (paypalcommercecreditcards, with PayPal-hosted card fields) stays SELECTED underneath it, so the day store credit no longer covers the balance the overlay disappears and the same Place Order click would charge a real card. The 'Place Order' button (#checkout-payment-continue) is enabled with no interaction. Order placement is armed only by PLACE_ORDER=true + I_KNOW_THIS_PLACES_ORDERS=true in the PARENT process env plus this store's committed checkout.placeOrder flag; every order it creates must be cancelled by hand in the BigCommerce admin, and a failed armed run may leave an 'Incomplete' order that the admin's default filter hides.

customFields.note: 'Is this a construction site address? (Required)' — answering No. A BigCommerce custom shipping field: it carries NO `required` HTML attribute, only '(Required)' in its label text, so nothing in the DOM marks it mandatory — but leaving it blank silently stops the carrier quote and no shipping options ever render.
